title: Stress-Testing Agent-Identity Standards Against Real Multi-Agent Interaction Traces

original_idea.body:
# Stress-Testing Agent-Identity Standards Against Real Multi-Agent Interaction Traces

**Problem:** The 'AI Identity: Standards, Gaps' paper catalogues gaps in agent identity/authorization standards (static scopes vs. dynamic context-dependent permissions) but does not test the gaps against actual multi-agent interaction logs.

**Direction:** Run a small open-source multi-agent framework on benign tasks to generate interaction traces, then attempt to apply the paper's identity/attribution requirements to the logs: can you reconstruct which agent did what and who is accountable? Report concrete failures where current identity primitives are insufficient.

**Why it matters:** Attribution and accountability for inter-agent actions is foundational governance infrastructure for the agentic era; demonstrating concrete failure modes is valuable prototype work doable outside any lab. Local agents, light compute.

**Relevant context:** Extends 'AI Identity: Standards, Gaps, and...' (arXiv:2604.23280, April 2026), testing its identified identity/authorization gaps against generated multi-agent traces.
